test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for Simple Interest multiples: T₂ = [(n₂ − 1) ÷ (n₁ − 1)] × T₁

Given n₁ = 7, T₁ = 14 years, and n₂ = 18.

T₂ = [(18 − 1) ÷ (7 − 1)] × 14 = (17 ÷ 6) × 14

T₂ = (17 × 7) ÷ 3 = 119 ÷ 3 = 39.666... ≈ 39.67

**∴ The correct answer is 39.67 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial sum = P

Amount after 14 years (A₁) = 7P

Target Amount (A₂) = 18P

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = Amount − Principal

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
 
 P
 7P
 14 Years
 Interest = 6P
 
 
 
 P
 18P
 T = ? Years
 Interest = 17P
 Rate (R) is constant in both cases

**Calculations:**

**Case 1:**

⇒ Interest (I₁) = 7P − P = 6P

⇒ 6P = (P × R × 14) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (6P × 100) ÷ (14 × P) = 600 ÷ 14 = 300 ÷ 7 %

**Case 2:**

⇒ Interest (I₂) = 18P − P = 17P

⇒ 17P = (P × R × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ 17P = [P × (300 ÷ 7) × T₂] ÷ 100

⇒ 17 = (3 × T₂) ÷ 7

⇒ T₂ = (17 × 7) ÷ 3 = 119 ÷ 3

⇒ T₂ = 39.666... years

⇒ T₂ ≈ 39.67 years

**∴ The correct answer is 39.67 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation for Simple Interest Multiples

If a sum becomes 'n' times itself in 'T' years at simple interest, the rate of interest is given by R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Simple vs Compound Interest Concept

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for each year. In Compound Interest, the interest gets added to the principal and acts as the new principal for the next period.

Rule of 72

A general estimation trick used in finance: to find the approximate number of years it takes to double your money at a given compound interest rate 'R', divide 72 by R.
